newsitem.title: NORWAY: Russia to consult NATO on new Bosnia force.
newsitem.headline: Russia to consult NATO on new Bosnia force.

text.p: Russia is ready to start immediate consultations with NATO on the possibility of sending a new international military peacekeeping force to Bosnia next year, Russian Defence Minister Igor Rodionov, said on Thursday.
Rodionov made the comment to reporters after talks with NATO defence ministers at a meeting in Bergen.

"Russia is ready to immediately start consultations with the allies in regard to agreement on the whole political and military aspects of possible continuation of (the) operation in Bosnia," said Rodionov.
NATO Secretary General Javier Solana, at a joint news conference with Rodionov, welcomed the move, saying that "we are going to continue working together in planning for post-IFOR."
Russia currently has troops in Bosnia as part of a NATO-led force of 52,000 international troops.

The NATO defence ministers, who wound up a two-day meeting on Thursday, ordered alliance military officials to study alternatives for a possible new force next year to keep the peace after the current peace implementation force (IFOR) ends its mandate this December 20.
